ca_convocation_boulder.blurb: Convocation Boulder is a single block next to the walking road into the Emeralds, in the Bowman Lake Road area near Lake Tahoe, at roughly 4,500 feet. It has eight problems, all on the gentle side: one is V-easy and the rest run up to about V2. Tree cover keeps it shaded, which helps on warm days. Plenty of climbers pass it on the way to the sport walls and the river, so it works as a short warm-up stop or a first boulder session for someone new to the sport.

ca_log_boulder.blurb: Log Boulder is a small bouldering spot in the Rick's Rocks cluster above Mammoth Lakes, in the Eastern Sierra at about 7,900 feet. Its eight problems, labeled A through H, are mostly easy: one at VB, four at V0 and three at V1. Landings are flat and the holds are generally good, although the tops of the climbs collect some dirt. The surrounding Southern Edge section stays shaded through the morning and early afternoon. This makes a handy first stop to loosen up before moving to the steeper boulders nearby.
ca_log_boulder.approach: From the parking area, go left and down the drainage. A fallen log lies across a couple of boulders, and Log Boulder is just beyond it.

ca_looking_wall.blurb: Looking Wall is a west-facing sport cliff in the Eastern Sierra near Mammoth Lakes, at about 7,500 feet. It holds eight bolted routes on short, steep, overhanging faces: one at 5.9, three at 5.10, three at 5.11 and one at 5.12. The wall stays in shade until around 2 pm, so it suits summer afternoons, and it catches evening sun early or late in the season. The drive in is long and on dirt, and the cliff comes into view across a small stream once you leave the parking spot. Pick a route within your grade, as the spread is narrow and sits mostly in the middle grades.

ca_bear_s_lair_the.blurb: The Bear's Lair is a compact sport area in the Benches section of the Emeralds, near Lake Tahoe at about 4,600 feet. It has eight bolted routes, short and steep, from 5.9 up through 5.12: one 5.9, five at 5.11 and two at 5.12. Shade holds here until late afternoon, which is useful when the weather is warm. Boulder problems can also be found around the same walls. With few routes at the lower grades, it suits climbers already comfortable on steep, powerful ground.

ca_main_boulder.blurb: Main Boulder is the biggest single block at the Fort Ross beach bouldering area on the Sonoma Coast, standing about 20 feet tall. Its eight problems divide into two camps: an easy slab on the right, and a fully overhung left side where the problems run from around V5 up to V10. Starts are rough and finishes are high, so a pad and spotters matter. Landings are soft sand in summer, but the sand level drops in winter and changes both the landings and which problems can be done. The ocean is close by if you need to cool off.
ca_main_boulder.approach: Take the path from the parking lot down to the beach, turn left and follow the sand to the large boulder at the far end.

ca_main_wall_lower_left.blurb: Main Wall - Lower Left is the lower-left section of the Main Wall at High Eagle, a sport crag on the western slope of the southern Sierra in the Shuteye Ridge area, at about 7,000 feet. It has eight routes, six of them sport and two trad, from 5.9 to 5.11 with five at 5.10. A few lines need gear. The wall faces east, so it gets morning sun and falls into shade by mid-afternoon. Reach it by walking down the slabs below High Eagle, passing the Shape Shifter area first and making a step-across move.

ca_mary_worth_buttress.blurb: Mary Worth Buttress is the first tall crag on the way to the Comic Strip formation, in the Comic Book Area of Joshua Tree National Park, at about 4,400 feet. Eight routes climb its face: five trad and three top rope, from 5.9 to 5.10, with seven of them at 5.10. One line is two pitches. The face points southwest and takes a lot of sun, so an early start helps. The base is reached by leaving the main trail, passing just left of some big boulders, then climbing the hillside on a faint path.

ca_kudos_left.blurb: Kudos Left is the left half of Kudos Cliff, a steep, powerful face in the Benches section of the Emeralds near Lake Tahoe, at about 4,800 feet. It has eight routes, mostly bolted sport lines, plus one that can be top-roped and one that is top rope only. Grades run from 5.6 up to 5.12, with the weight at the harder end: three at 5.12 and two at 5.11.
